operator: hostapd 2.11 in an OrbStack Ubuntu VM; Location Services-enabled CoreWLAN scan from macOS

console.model_source: owner manual confirmation; PTP DeviceInfo reports the generic model 'Nintendo Switch'
console.firmware_observation_note: The console was not involved in this control test.
console.modification_source: owner report; this test does not detect modifications

commands.command: sudo ip link set <interface> down; sudo iw dev <interface> set type managed; sudo ip link set <interface> up
commands.result: The adapter was switched from monitor mode to managed mode.
hostapd ran until the 30-second timeout. Its log reached 'AP-ENABLED' and later 'AP-DISABLED' on termination.
The test SSID TX10LED-TEST was visible at -32 dBm on channel 1, with the host adapter BSSID. The hostapd log confirms AP-ENABLED.

commands.command: sudo pkill -x hostapd; restore monitor mode on channel 1
commands.result: hostapd stopped and the adapter was restored to monitor mode on channel 1.

ap_test.receiver: macOS CoreWLAN wildcard scan with Location Services authorization

interpretation: The adapter and the in-kernel rtw88_8822bu driver can transmit a normal 2.4 GHz AP beacon on channel 1. The Mac received it at -32 dBm with the adapter's BSSID. This is a positive control for the monitor-mode test: the RF path and the adapter's AP-mode TX path work, so a failure in monitor mode is specific to monitor-mode injection, not to the hardware's ability to transmit.
authorization: The owner approved a normal AP-mode transmission test on channel 1 with a test SSID. The test did not touch the console and did not send LDN frames.
limitations: One adapter, one driver, one kernel, and one channel.
The test transmitted a normal AP beacon, not an LDN beacon or vendor action frame.
The Mac scan is a reception check, not a frame capture.
The host adapter BSSID is redacted.
redactions: Interface name redacted because it is derived from the adapter MAC.
